questions.question: What is the LCM of 15 and 25?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Numbers: 15 and 25

**Concept:**

The Least Common Multiple (LCM) of two numbers is the smallest number that is a multiple of both.

**Solution:**

⇒ Find the prime factorization of 15: 3 × 5

⇒ Find prime factorization of 25: 5 × 5

⇒ LCM is the product of the highest powers of all prime numbers: 3¹ × 5² = 75

**Therefore, the LCM of 15 and 25 is 75.**

questions.question: If both length and breadth of a cuboid is increased by 50 percent, then by how much percent its height should be reduced so that its volume remains same?
questions.solution:
**Given**

The length and breadth of a cuboid are increased by 50%.

**Concept: **The volume of a cuboid is given by Volume = Length × Breadth × Height. We want to keep the volume

constant.

**Solution:**

⇒ Initial volume V1 = L × B × H

⇒ Final volume V2 = 1.5L × 1.5B × H2 (H2 is the new height)

⇒ For V1 = V2, we get 1.5 × 1.5 × H2 = L × B × H

⇒ Solving for H2, we get H2 = (L × B × H)/(1.5 × 1.5) = H/2.25

⇒ The reduction in height = H - H2 = H - (H/2.25) = H (1 - 1/2.25) = H × 0.5555 = 55.55% of H

**Therefore, the height should be reduced by 55.55 percent.**

questions.question: The average of p, q, r and s is 30. If the average of p and q is 12. then what will be the average of r and s?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Average of p, q, r, s = 30

Average of p, q = 12

**Concept:**

The average is the sum of the numbers divided by the count.

**Solution:**

⇒ Sum of p, q, r, s = Average × count = 30 × 4 = 120

⇒ Sum of p, q = Average × count = 12 × 2 = 24

⇒ Sum of r, s = Sum of p, q, r, s - Sum of p, q = 120 - 24 = 96

⇒ Average of r, s = Sum of r, s/count = 96/2 = 48

**Therefore, the average of r and s is 48.**

questions.question: M alone can complete a work in 50 days and N alone can complete the same work in 100 days. If both of them work together, then in 25 days what percent work of the total work will be completed?
questions.solution:
**Given**

M can complete a work in 50 days.

N can complete the same work in 100 days.

Both work together for 25 days.

**Concept:**

The work completed is the product of rate and time.

**Solution:**

⇒ Rate of M = 1/50 per day, rate of N = 1/100 per day.

⇒ Rate of M and N together = rate of M + rate of N = 1/50 + 1/100 = 3/100 per day.

⇒ Work completed in 25 days = Rate × time = 3/100 × 25 = 0.75 = 75%

**Therefore, 75% of the total work will be completed in 25 days.**

questions.question: A saves 18% of his income. If his income increases by 41% and still saves the same amount, Find the percentage Increase In his expenditure.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let initial Income = 100. Then Savings = 18 and Expenditure = 82.

Income increases by 41% (100 → 141). The savings amount remains the same (18).

Since Income = Expenditure + Savings, the entire increase in income must go to expenditure if savings is constant.

Increase in Expenditure = Income Increase = 41.

% Increase in Expenditure = (Increase ÷ Original Expenditure) × 100 = (41 ÷ 82) × 100 = 50%.

**∴ The correct answer is 50%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Savings = 18% of Income

Income Increase = 41%

Final Savings = Initial Savings (Amount)

**Formula:**

Income = Expenditure + Savings

Percentage Increase = (Change ÷ Original Value) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4e310adb63269585c7833c4d76c625c5e0c0415b1d0d08a3999191eac7cccb1c.png] 

⇒ Let original income = 100

⇒ Original Savings = 18

⇒ Original Expenditure = 100 − 18 = 82

⇒ New Income = 100 + 41% of 100 = 141

⇒ New Savings = 18 (amount remains constant)

⇒ New Expenditure = 141 − 18 = 123

⇒ Increase in Expenditure = 123 − 82 = 41

⇒ Percentage Increase = (41 ÷ 82) × 100

⇒ Percentage Increase = 1/2 × 100 = 50%

**∴ The correct answer is 50%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income-Expenditure Components

Income is the sum of Expenditure and Savings. A change in any one component must be balanced by the others to satisfy the equation: ΔIncome = ΔExpenditure + ΔSavings.

Percentage Change Formula

To find the percentage increase or decrease, always use the initial value as the base: % Change = [(New Value − Old Value) ÷ Old Value] × 100.

Effect of Constant Component

If savings remains constant (ΔSavings = 0), then the absolute increase in income is exactly equal to the absolute increase in expenditure.</p

questions.question: A bus covers a distance of 45 km in 45 minutes. If its speed is decreased by 20 km/hr, then what will be the time taken by it to cover the same distance?
questions.solution:
**Given Data:**

Distance = 45 km

Initial time = 45 minutes

Speed decreased by 20 km/hr

**Concept: **Time = Distance/Speed

**Solution:**

⇒ Initial speed = Distance/time = 45 km/(45 min/60) hr = 60 km/hr

⇒ Reduced speed = Initial speed - reduction = 60 km/hr - 20 km/hr = 40 km/hr

⇒ New time = Distance/Reduced speed = 45 km/40 km/hr = 1.125 hr = 67.5 min

**Therefore, the new time taken to cover the same distance is 67.5 minutes.**

questions.question: A man earns a profit of 45 percent by selling a bike for a certain price. If he sells that bike at double the price, then what will be the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the Cost Price (CP) of the bike be 100 units.

Selling Price (SP) at 45% profit = 100 + 45 = 145 units.

New SP when sold at double the price = 2 × 145 = 290 units.

New Profit = New SP − CP = 290 − 100 = 190 units.

Since the base CP is 100 units, the profit percentage is directly the profit amount.

**∴ The correct answer is 190%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial profit percentage = 45%

New Selling Price = 2 × Initial Selling Price

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100

Profit% = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/90b9a6846371864149e30d5fa1d627c2df919edb190e25b3ee31a3d6ae01c63a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the Cost Price (CP) of the bike be x.

⇒ Initial Selling Price (SP) = x × (100 + 45) ÷ 100 = 1.45x

⇒ New Selling Price = 2 × Initial SP = 2 × 1.45x = 2.90x

⇒ New Profit = New Selling Price − CP

⇒ New Profit = 2.90x − x = 1.90x

⇒ New Profit % = (New Profit ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ New Profit % = (1.90x ÷ x) × 100 = 190%

**∴ The correct answer is 190%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

MP is the price printed on the article. Discount is always calculated on the MP. Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

Successive Profit

When an article is sold sequentially by multiple sellers, the effective SP is calculated cumulatively: Final SP = CP × (100 + P₁%) ÷ 100 × (100 + P₂%) ÷ 100.

Dishonest Dealer

When a dealer professes to sell goods at CP but uses a false weight, the profit percentage is calculated as: Profit % = (Error ÷ (True Value − Error)) × 100.
</p

• These are typically less serious offences against the **State or individuals**.

• Cross offences occur when two or more parties involved in an incident both allege** criminal offences against each other.**
 
• For instance, in a physical altercation, both parties might claim that the other party was the aggressor and they themselves were **acting in self-defence**.
